content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on efficient semantic segmentation and proposes a pruning method to solve for an efficient network. Specifically, the paper focuses on vision transformers. Pruning is achieved by solving a bi-level optimization problem that solves a binary mask to find the small number of layers. The model is evaluated on segmentation tasks and achieves good performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- It is well motivated to obtain a small network with pruned parameters by solving a bi-level optimization problem. 
- The performance on segmentation tasks proves the efficiency of the proposed approaches.
- The paper is easy to follow.  

Weakness
- The paper claims the proposed method is for semantic segmentation. However, the techniques are not specified for the application. It is more like an application of a general bi-level model pruning method on the specific application. If the bi-level optimization-based pruning is the first time proposed in the paper, in this context, many problems need to be addressed:
    - The sensitivities of the model to different setups like hyperparameters should be compared.
    - The related methods for model pruning should be discussed and compared, such as
        - Sehwag, Vikash, Shiqi Wang, Prateek Mittal, and Suman Jana. "Hydra: Pruning adversarially robust neural networks." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (2020): 19655-19666.
        - Wang, Chaoqi, Guodong Zhang, and Roger Grosse. "Picking winning tickets before training by preserving gradient flow." arXiv preprint arXiv:2002.07376 (2020).
    - If it is general for different base networks, the authors may conduct studies to apply the proposed method to different base networks.

- How is the threshold \tau set? The author may study the sensitivity to this parameter. This should be related to the strength or percentage of the pruning usually.
- It is not discussed the motivation for introducing bi-level optimization (BLO) for pruning, especially for segmentation. What are the advantages compared to other methods?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The whole paper is clear and easy to follow. 

However, many details about the bi-level optimization, including implementation and theoretical details, are not introduced and discussed, which may influence reproducibility. 
The techniques are not discussed and studied in a suitable context. 

**Additional notes**:
The proposed method seems with high relevance to another recent work:
- Zhang, Yihua, Yuguang Yao, Parikshit Ram, Pu Zhao, Tianlong Chen, Mingyi Hong, Yanzhi Wang, and Sijia Liu. "Advancing Model Pruning via Bi-level Optimization." NeurIPS (2022).

I do not want to ask the authors to cite this paper, since it seems to be released on arxiv later than the submission deadline.
content.summary_of_the_review: As discussed in the weakness points and *the above block*, the techniques of the whole paper seem not introduced and discussed in a proper context. The techniques are for general model pruning, with no specification for semantic segmentation. Many necessary technical details of BLO are not discussed.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper adopts a pruning parameterization method based on channel pruning to prune a segmentation model – TopFormer via a depth-conv layer and soft-mask optimization. The proposed method seems technically novel for edge-device model pruning. The proposed soft-mask binarization which can not be back-propagated and updated by the network training is solved by shifting the gradient of the hard-binary mask to the soft-mask layer. Further, the authors adopt a Bi-level Optimization to theoretical proof their model training can save computation resources. The experimental results regarding the segmentation performance and latency on mobile devices are impressive. The authors also validate their superior performance on various benchmarks to demonstrate their method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros
1.	The utilization of the depth-conv layer to perform channel pruning is a novel point. The proposed soft-mask can be optimized to search the channels that can be pruned or preserved for the final model status.
2.	The non-differential binary operation is further solved by gradient shifting and Bi-level Optimization, and the theoretical proof seems convincing.
3.	The final model performance on segmentation and latency is impressive on mobile devices, like Samsung S21.

Cons
1.	The choice of thresholding t is kind of confusing and needs to be applied to more ablative studies to demonstrate why 0.5 works fine.
2.	The writing sentences below eq (14), “The pruned weights … the weight values”, seems to be contrary to the original hypothesis, that the weights contributing nothing to the loss still hold their gradients and can be recovered and contribute to the accuracy. But this implementation set their gradients to zero. The author should provide more expressions.
3.	The major concern of this paper is their generalization. This paper conduct experiments on TopFormer segmentation models only which can not be generalized to other models. What about other transformer-based light-weight architectures? What about CNN-based light-weight models? Such as some ViT/Human Design series models making comparisons in the main paper. More convincing experiments on other segmentation models should be conducted for demonstrating the generalization of the pruning parameterization methods.
4.	From the tables in the main paper, the adopted larger per-layer width TopFormer Baseline model is not present and I can not see the actual efficacy of the model pruning. Besides, More ablative studies should be present. Such as replacing the binary-operation with random or removing the depth-conv and enabling the soft-masks to choose the channels?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is easy to follow and has fair technical novelty. The reproducibility is hard to decide.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper propose s a  method to 
to derive ViTs with fewer computations and fast inference speed to facilitate the dense prediction of
semantic segmentation on edge devices. For that, a pruning parameterization
method has been to formulated to solve the pruning problem of semantic segmentation.
A bi-level optimization method is used to solve this problem with the help

Results are shown on 3 benchmark datasets, and compared with ~dozen SOA.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Overall, the analytics presented is nice and good to read.
Quite a bit of experimental results presented.

There are some issues:
The term "Pruning parameterization" is a bit confusing.

Are you pruning the parameters during training, or pruning the process of parameterization to reduce cost (say) itself?
The former is well established, but the latter is doubtful (what that means ?).

The analytics presented in App. A - C are partly novel at the most. 
What about the convergence issue in Eqn. (15) - using bi-level optimization ?

Quite a few literature not cited, some given below (make a thorough search yourself):

Advancing Model Pruning via Bi-level Optimization; Yihua Zhang et. al; NIPS 2022.

DYNAMICALLY PRUNING SEGFORMER FOR EFFICIENT SEMANTIC SEGMENTATION; Haoli Bai et. al; https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.09499

Sparsity in Deep Learning: Pruning and growth for efficient inference and training in neural networks; Torsten Hoefler et. al ; Journal of Machine Learning Research 23 (2021) 1-124; 

Enable Deep Learning on Mobile Devices: Methods, Systems, and Applications; Han Cai et al.; ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems; Vol. 27, No. 3; pp 1–50; https://doi.org/10.1145/3486618

Bilevel Optimization: Convergence Analysis and Enhanced Design; Kaiyi Ji, Junjie Yang, Yingbin Liang; https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07962

Understanding Straight-Through Estimator in Training Activation Quantized Neural Nets; Penghang Yin, Jiancheng Lyu, Shuai Zhang, Stanley Osher, Yingyong Qi, Jack Xin; ICLR – 2019; https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05662

Finally, would have been nice if a few failure cases were illustrated and discussed.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Paper is easy to read and clear.
Quality is somewhat acceptale.

Not convinced that a majority of the work done is novel.

Ablation studies and results appears to be reproducible.
Not checked thoroughly though.

content.title: Pruning Parameterization with Bi-level Optimization for Efficient Semantic Segmentation on the Edge
content.TL;DR: We proposed a pruning parameterization method for real-time semantic segmentation on the edge.
content.abstract: With the ever-increasing popularity of edge devices, it is necessary to implement real-time segmentation on the edge for autonomous driving and many other applications. Vision Transformers (ViTs) have shown considerably stronger results for many vision tasks. However, ViTs with the full-attention mechanism usually consume a large number of computational resources, leading to difficulties for real-time inference on edge devices. In this paper, we aim to derive ViTs with fewer computations and fast inference speed to facilitate the dense prediction of semantic segmentation on edge devices. To achieve this, we propose a pruning parameterization method to formulate the pruning problem of semantic segmentation. Then we adopt a bi-level optimization method to solve this problem with the help of implicit gradients. Our experimental results demonstrate that we can achieve 38.9 mIoU on ADE20K val with a speed of 56.5 FPS on Samsung S21, which is the highest mIoU under the same computation constraint with real-time inference.
